question: can mixed exemplars restore the reference name on no-name inputs while keeping the syntax gain

arms.ctl: aug-r1 experiment pools unchanged (11 of 12 values carry the name)
arms.mix: same 12 targets byte for byte; six inputs rewritten without the name in the value

start: moved (bd5434b3), evaluated alongside; exp (e3de7659) is the previous arm and is quoted from its archive

devSets.namepair: 12 paired probes (6 pairs), r4 three checks

bothSides.rule: on the 12 namepair probes the mix arm passes at least 10 of 12 under the r4 checks, AND at least 5 of 6 on each side separately
bothSides.why: no start arm is good on both halves at once: moved passes 6/6 without the name and 0/6 with it (prefix duplicates), exp passes 1/6 without it and 6/6 with it (name dropped)

notNameOnly.rule: relation kept at least 11 of 12 and syntax broken at most 1 across all 12 probes

relationProbes.rule: at least 7 of 10 pass under r4

regression.fact: human count on cf24+final24+moved24 at or above the start arm 184/185
regression.language: not above the start arm (3 on cf24)
regression.machine: S/REV/A recorded per set and arm; the fact gate uses the human count, a new-round rule that does not rewrite earlier judgements

acceptance.overall: all of the above must hold; any single regression blocks a pass

notClaimed: the namepair design cannot separate form from length, so a pass here is a statement about this intervention, not proof that input length is irrelevant
